    The radical-square-zero category of a bipartite quiver #

    For a finite quiver given by src tgt : E → V in which no arrow ends where an arrow starts, the category RSZ src tgt has the vertices as objects; its morphisms are the identities, the arrows and zero, and every composite of two arrows is zero. It is a finite ray category (RayCat.RSZ.isRayCategory). For the alternating cycle it is the crown category used to show that crowns make algebras representation-infinite.
